name: Brazil: Minas, Bahia and the Chapada
tagline: Baroque gold towns, Afro-Brazilian Salvador, and dry-season trekking in the Chapada Diamantina.

access.route: Brussels→Rio or São Paulo via Lisbon, Paris or Amsterdam (TAP, Air France, KLM), 12–13 h; internal flights on top
London→Rio or São Paulo direct (BA, LATAM), 11.5 h

nightsNote: 10–14°C in the Chapada and Minas towns, 18°C in Rio and Salvador
whyNotes: The other Latin America option, and the one with the right season: July and August are the dry southern winter, 22–27°C, no altitude anywhere, and the Chapada Diamantina trek is as good as Ciudad Perdida with cabins instead of hammocks.
fitNotes: Easy on Mom's three limits except Rio, which is crowded; keep it to two days. The cost is distance: you fly between regions, which adds about €270 of internal flights and some airport days.

blocks.name: Rio de Janeiro
blocks.place: MAR, Museu do Amanhã, Santa Teresa, Tijuca forest
blocks.history: Imperial capital, port of the slave trade
see: Museu de Arte do Rio and Museu do Amanhã on the renewed port
Valongo wharf (UNESCO) and Little Africa walking tour
Santa Teresa and the Selarón steps early
Pedra Bonita or Dois Irmãos walk instead of the Christ queue
blocks.note: Crowded and expensive by Brazilian standards. Two days, and arrive here or leave from here.

blocks.name: Ouro Preto + Mariana
see: São Francisco de Assis and Pilar churches
blocks.note: Hilly cobbles everywhere; good shoes. Fly Rio–Belo Horizonte 1 h, then 2 h.

blocks.name: Tiradentes + São João del-Rei
blocks.place: Quietest of the colonial towns, Maria Fumaça steam train
see: Maria Fumaça steam train to São João del-Rei
Serra de São José trail above the town

blocks.name: Belo Horizonte + Inhotim
blocks.place: The largest open-air contemporary art park in the world
see: Inhotim pavilions in a botanical garden (full day)

blocks.name: Salvador da Bahia
see: Pelourinho and São Francisco church (gold interior)
Capoeira and a candomblé evening with a local host
Mercado Modelo and the Lacerda elevator

blocks.name: Paraty
blocks.place: Colonial port of the gold road, schooner bay
see: Caminho do Ouro stone road walk

blocks.name: Chapada Diamantina
blocks.place: Vale do Pati trek, Fumaça waterfall, Pai Inácio
see: Vale do Pati 3-day trek sleeping in farmhouses (guide mandatory)
Cachoeira da Fumaça from the top
Morro do Pai Inácio at sunset
Lençóis town, Poço Azul blue cave
blocks.note: Dry season, 25°C days, cold nights. Reach Lençóis by 1 h flight from Salvador or 6 h bus.

blocks.name: Serra do Cipó
blocks.place: Highland savanna, waterfalls, 1,300 m, near Belo Horizonte

blocks.name: Itatiaia National Park
blocks.place: Brazil's oldest park, Atlantic forest to 2,700 m plateau
see: Lower park waterfalls and forest trails

blocks.name: Ilha Grande
blocks.place: Car-free island, forest trails to empty beaches
see: Abraão to Dois Rios old prison walk

blocks.name: Serra da Canastra
blocks.place: Source of the São Francisco, Casca d'Anta falls, cheese country
see: Casca d'Anta waterfall from above and below
São Roque de Minas cheese farms

notes: Dry winter season in Minas, Bahia and the Chapada: 22–27°C, cold clear nights.
Rio can get a cold front: 18°C and rain for two days. Keep Rio flexible.
Brazilian school holidays run to late July; the Chapada and Paraty are busier before 1 August.

lodgingAssumption: Local B&B or Airbnb, two rooms for five, one meal out a day; shared van or hire car
